findings.claim: Removing the unconditional per-request setAttribute calls also removes the incidental per-request dirty-marking of the HttpSession, so authorization-relevant state that is mutated in place on the session-stored UserContext (refreshAuthenticatedUser reloading roles/privileges, removeProxyPrivilege, setLocationId) may no longer be persisted or replicated by session stores that only save on attribute change; was a clustered / externally-stored-session deployment considered?
findings.evidence: The UserContext is written to the session only on creation (OpenmrsFilter.java:76-81, unchanged); every later change is an in-place mutation of that same object. api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/UserContext.java:50 declares `public class UserContext implements Serializable`, so it is intended to survive a replicating/persisting session store, and lines 152 (refreshAuthenticatedUser -> reloads the User, i.e. roles and privileges, without changing getUsername()), 264/319 (removeProxyPrivilege) and 578 (setLocationId) all mutate authorization-relevant state without changing the `username` or `locale` values this PR now compares against. Before this change every request executed `setAttribute("username", ...)` and `setAttribute("locale", ...)` (base version, git show eda229b1:.../OpenmrsFilter.java lines 75 and 94), which marked the session dirty every request; at d381957e a steady-state request performs zero writes -- I confirmed this empirically with a probe extending BaseWebContextSensitiveTest that recorded setAttribute calls (second request on an unchanged authenticated session: writes=[]; the PR's own OpenmrsFilterTest#doFilterInternal_shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes asserts the same, 5/5 green via `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest`). Counter-evidence I found and am reporting honestly: `git grep -n distributable` over the tree returns nothing (positive control: the same `git grep` pipeline finds 'anonymous user' in 4 files), webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:375-379 has a session-config with only a cookie-config, `git grep -in 'session replicat|PersistentManager|DeltaManager|BackupManager|spring-session|SessionRepository'` returns nothing, and the TRUNK-6701 description itself frames the redundant locale write as a *problem* ('marking the session dirty for replicating session managers'). Also, per-attribute delta managers (Tomcat DeltaManager, Spring Session's delta map) only ever replicated the `username`/`locale` keys, never the userContext key, so for those the gap pre-dates this PR; it is only full-session-on-dirty managers (e.g. Tomcat BackupManager) where this is a change.

what_i_swept:
Verified the diff first: `git diff eda229b12a28a41ba35ecd75b910803da93631a8 d381957e84386f5902bec7886b8f2ba391dc5101` = 3 files, +279/-12, matching the briefing. Read all three files in full at d381957e plus the base version of OpenmrsFilter.java, and read the TRUNK-6701 ticket via the unauthenticated JIRA REST endpoint (summary/description/status/2 comments).

INPUT VALIDATION / INJECTION / DESERIALIZATION: the diff parses no request input. The only values flowing into the new code are `user.getUsername()` (DB-sourced) and `userContext.getLocale()`; both are compared with Objects.equals and stored as session attributes. No SQL, no command construction, no rendering, no new (de)serialization surface -- the only pre-existing deserialization read (the UserContext attribute, line 73) is untouched. The csrfguard cache-header block (lines 96-103) is byte-identical and still ordered after the attribute writes, so the filter's position relative to CSRFGuard is unchanged.

AUTHORIZATION: the filter makes no authorization decision; `Context.setUserContext(userContext)` / `Context.clearUserContext()` (lines 106 and 115) are unchanged, so the thread-bound authentication contract is untouched. I proved the end state of the two attributes is identical to the base version for every reachable combination by case analysis and then by running two probes (a temporary ZzSecProbeTest extending BaseWebContextSensitiveTest, since deleted): (a) authenticate as test_user, run the filter, call UserContext.logout() WITHOUT invalidating the session, run the filter again -> username correctly resets to '-anonymous user-' with exactly one write, so a logged-out session does not keep advertising the authenticated username; (b) a UserContext whose authenticated User has a null username (systemId-only users) -> setAttribute(name, null) removes the attribute, matching the base behaviour rather than leaving a stale previous username. Both probes passed, which falsified the stale-identity finding I was developing. I also read UserContext.logout() (line 227: nulls user, locationId, locale and clears proxies) and becomeUser() (line 171) to confirm every identity switch changes getUsername() and therefore still triggers a write.

SECRETS: the only new resource is web/src/test/resources/OpenmrsFilterTest-initial.xml. Its single <users> row is a verbatim copy of an existing fixture -- identical user_id=5506, person_id=501, system_id, username, password hash, salt and uuid to api/src/test/resources/org/openmrs/api/include/AdministrationServiceTest-globalproperties.xml:27 and EncounterServiceTest-initialData.xml:95 -- and the hash/salt pair is the long-standing OpenMRS test credential also used for `admin` in initialInMemoryTestDataSet.xml:18 and asserted in api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/util/SecurityTest.java:52. So no new secret is introduced, the plaintext ('test') is a published test fixture, and the row grants no roles. No CI/workflow/pom files are touched by the PR at all.

TRACE OUTWARD (one level past the changed lines): (1) CONSUMERS of the two attributes -- `git grep -n -E 'getAttribute\(\s*"(username|locale)"|setAttribute\(\s*"(username|locale)"'` finds ZERO readers or writers in any main source set, only three test hits (InitializationFilterE2ETest:109, UpdateFilterE2ETest:101,363). Broadening to constants found web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/util/FilterUtil.java:36 `LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE = "locale"`, written as a String (not a Locale) by InitializationFilter:995-1021 and UpdateFilter:195-301 -- same key, different type, so the new equality check can never match across those writers, which is harmless but noted. There are no JSPs left in this repo (`find webapp/src/main/webapp -name '*.jsp'` = 0), so any remaining reader lives in legacyui, out of repo -- and since the attribute VALUES are provably unchanged, such a reader is unaffected. (2) LISTENERS -- web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java:78 is the only session listener in the tree; it implements HttpSessionListener (sessionCreated/sessionDestroyed at lines 153-170, fanned out to Spring components via Context.getRegisteredComponents at line 183) and NOT HttpSessionAttributeListener, so no core-registered component observed the per-request attribute writes. (3) LIFECYCLE / SESSION STORE -- this is where security-1 comes from: the per-request writes were the only thing marking the session dirty, and I traced which UserContext mutators change authorization state without changing username or locale. (4) UNCHANGED NEIGHBOURS -- OpenmrsFilter.java:71-72 still claims the usercontext storage logic is mirrored in 'webinf/view/uncaughtexception.jsp' to keep stack traces from unauthenticated users; that file does not exist in this repo, and the PR does not change the UserContext-on-session logic it refers to, so the information-disclosure control it describes is not weakened. (5) SESSION CREATION -- httpRequest.getSession() at line 61 is unchanged, satisfying the ticket's explicit 'session creation behavior must not change' constraint, so no session-fixation or session-flooding surface moved.

Three passes: pass 1 case-analysis of old vs new end state plus secrets/injection/authz sweep; pass 2 outward trace (consumers, listeners, other writers of the same keys, clustering config) which surfaced security-1; pass 3 empirical probes of the logout and null-username transitions, which surfaced nothing substantive, so the sweep converged.

out_of_scope: Solution fit: TRUNK-6701 asks to 'remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute', but OpenmrsFilter.java:64 still unconditionally does httpRequest.setAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID, String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis())) at head -- that half of the ticket is unaddressed while the ticket is Closed.

Correctness/consistency: FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE (web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/util/FilterUtil.java:36) is the same 'locale' session key, but InitializationFilter:995-1021 and UpdateFilter:195-301 store a String there while OpenmrsFilter stores a Locale, so the new equality check can never match immediately after setup/update and the redundant write persists in exactly that window.

Test isolation: OpenmrsFilter's finally block calls Context.clearUserContext(), so invoking doFilterInternal from a BaseWebContextSensitiveTest wipes the test thread's own UserContext mid-method; the five new tests happen to survive this but it is a latent fragility for anyone extending the class.
Stale comment: OpenmrsFilter.java:71-72 points at 'webinf/view/uncaughtexception.jsp', which no longer exists in this repo (0 .jsp files under webapp/src/main/webapp).

Test coverage: no test exercises the authenticated -> logged-out transition on a surviving session, which is the behaviourally interesting one; I verified it manually with a throwaway probe and it is correct, but it is unguarded against regression.
could_not_verify: Could not stand up a clustered or externally-stored session (Tomcat BackupManager/DeltaManager with SimpleTcpCluster, Tomcat PersistentManager, or Spring Session Redis) to confirm or refute whether dropping the per-request attribute writes actually stops in-place UserContext mutations from being persisted or replicated. That is the single experiment that would settle security-1, which is why it ships as a low-confidence question rather than an issue.

Could not check downstream consumers outside openmrs-core (legacyui and reference-application modules) for readers of the 'username' / 'locale' session attributes; this repo has zero main-code readers and zero JSPs. The argument that they are unaffected rests on the attribute values being provably unchanged, which I did verify, not on having read those consumers.

Could not observe a container-level HttpSessionAttributeListener or APM agent reacting to the (now absent) per-request attributeReplaced events; core registers no such listener, but an operator-installed one would silently stop seeing per-request username/locale events.
notes: Short report is the honest answer here: this PR barely touches the security dimension. It adds no input handling, no authorization logic, no secrets and no deserialization, and I positively verified that the end state of both session attributes is identical to the base version on every path I could reach, including the two transitions the PR's own tests do not cover (logout on a surviving session, and an authenticated user with a null username). The one genuine security-adjacent consequence is that the session is no longer marked dirty on every request, which is exactly what the ticket asked for -- so security-1 is framed as a question to the maintainers about clustered deployments, not as a defect. I deliberately did not manufacture additional findings to fill the lens. Verification notes: `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` -> Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 at d381957e. A temporary probe class (web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/ZzSecProbeTest.java) was created, run (2/2 green), and deleted; `git status --porcelain` in the worktree is empty and HEAD is still d381957e84. Every zero-hit search reported above was preceded by a positive control on the same pipeline (`git grep -c 'anonymous user'` returns hits in 4 files, while `git grep -n distributable` exits 1). Nothing was written to GitHub.
